title: Ectopic Pregnancy: Presentation and Diagnostic Approach
subject: OBG
preview: Ectopic pregnancy can present with amenorrhea, unilateral pain, vaginal bleeding or collapse from intra-abdominal hemorrhage.
quickRevision: Ectopic pregnancy can present with amenorrhea, unilateral pain, vaginal bleeding or collapse from intra-abdominal hemorrhage.
Serial quantitative hCG and transvaginal ultrasound are interpreted together and with clinical stability.
A pregnancy of unknown location needs a follow-up plan, not premature reassurance.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: Ectopic pregnancy can present with amenorrhea, unilateral pain, vaginal bleeding or collapse from intra-abdominal hemorrhage.
Any reproductive-age patient with concerning abdominal pain should have pregnancy status assessed where appropriate.

sections.title: Differentiate and manage
points: Serial quantitative hCG and transvaginal ultrasound are interpreted together and with clinical stability.
A pregnancy of unknown location needs a follow-up plan, not premature reassurance.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not delay emergency evaluation in a hemodynamically unstable patient while waiting for serial tests.
